name: Bazzle's workshop
description: The cluttered clock workshop filled with two hundred twelve clocks where the events take place.

timeline.summary: Bazzle wakes to a cry of alarm and realizes that his clockwork creation has escaped again.
timeline.quote: It got out again. My creation continues to defy my wishes!

timeline.summary: Bazzle recalls how he built his greatest creation, and finds strange objects and keys left in his shop.
timeline.quote: Mostly, he found strange keys, hundreds of them, filling small burlap sacks and stacked near the door.

timeline.summary: Bazzle finds a crude brass clockwork arm on his workbench and realizes it is made of melted keys.
timeline.quote: Keys. This is made of melted keys.

timeline.summary: Bazzle realizes the creature has learned its creator's trade and effectively become his apprentice.
timeline.quote: Now, it seemed, he finally had an apprentice.

timeline.summary: Bazzle tries to dislodge the creature's chest key, but the creature winds itself and strikes him in the face.
timeline.quote: Before Bazzle could do anything, the hand swung back and struck him squarely in the face.

timeline.summary: On the second morning Bazzle finds a severed clockwork head made from the guard's helmet, his own reading crystals and the stirrups and teeth.
As Bazzle crawls to the key, the creature strikes the back of his neck and slides the key into place.
timeline.quote: just as the thing's arm connected with the back of his neck.

timeline.summary: On the third morning Bazzle finds his good arm severed and the metal arm attached in its place.
timeline.quote: his formerly good arm lay severed on the floor near his bed

timeline.summary: Bazzle realizes the creature never wanted a companion or army, only to stop sharing a body with him.
timeline.quote: It had merely decided it would no longer share a body with a rotting old clockmaker.

timeline.summary: The creature takes a cleaver and beheads Bazzle, setting its own head in his place and completing itself.
timeline.quote: The last thing he saw was his shop spinning roof-over-floor around him.
